headline: Scaling Quantum Hardware, Circuits, and Anyon Simulations
summary: Today's research spans practical physical scaling across quantum hardware and computational modeling. Key highlights include improved surface-code memory on cloud superconducting chips, octave-spanning parametric amplification, and AI-driven breakthroughs in circuit compilation and anyonic wavefunctions.

themes.title: Hardware Realization & Error Suppression
themes.body: Demonstrations targeting high-fidelity physical systems, from suppressing logical errors in surface-code memory via pulse engineering to clean octave-wide gain in balanced TWPAs.

themes.title: Machine Learning for Quantum Optimization & Networking
themes.body: Leveraging machine learning as surrogates and optimizers to route noisy network channels and verify algorithmic circuit compression.

themes.title: Physics-Informed Circuit & Many-Body Learning
themes.body: Embedding explicit physical priors—such as fractional statistical boundaries or spectral transform queries—directly into quantum neural representations.

connections.body: Both papers embed rigorous physical structure directly into neural ansatzes—enforcing non-analytic anyonic boundary conditions in AnyNet and Fourier-aligned spectral biases in parameterized circuits.

Both approaches use classical ML surrogates to handle analytical intractability in quantum domains: verifying compiled subroutines via automated fuzzing and estimating complex multi-hop quantum network delays.
